## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

(Canonical criteria — promoted from the producer-approved re-scope of 2026-11-09; they supersede the original AC1–AC6 recorded below. Original AC6 includes the `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard, which C6 relocates and updates.)

- **P5. Tooling + docs** — test-skill type profiles (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) still run; comments, AGENTS.md and dev notes updated (CHANGELOG excluded — ship skill).
- **P6. Full suite passes.**

## Superseded original acceptance criteria (replaced 2026-11-09 by the P1–P6 re-scope above)

Retained for traceability only; NOT the completion gate — P1–P6 above are.

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and

4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles

5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any

6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is

- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).


---

## Proposal addendum — beat-locked soundtrack and intensity mix (2026-11-17 review)

Accepted as **planned** in the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 6 of
10 of that review's proposals). These requirements are **additive**: they do not
replace any acceptance criterion above.

1. **Beat lock to the shipped lattice.** The music's tempo is the run's
   `beatBpm` (default **80**, 187.5 ms per 16th-note step), not an independent
   tempo. Bars, phrases and transitions align to the *same* lattice every weapon
   already fires on (GDD §2.3), so player shots land on the beat by
   construction. A change to `beatBpm` retunes the music with no other edit, and
   the music can never drift from the fire grid.
2. **Intensity-driven stems, not track swaps.** One continuous musical bed whose
   layers gate on a **documented intensity parameter** derived from game state —
   menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-lives tension, run end — with layer
   entry and exit **on bar boundaries only** (never mid-bar), plus the stinger
   and ducking rules the Audio Design Chapter already defines. The parameter is
   computed from scene state in **one pure helper**, so it is testable,
   reproducible and identical in game and gym.
3. **Never fight the mix.** Music sits under the baked SFX (`docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`),
   carries its own volume separate from the shipped SFX volume/mute settings,
   ducks during boss entrances and power-up fanfares, and degrades to a safe
   no-op without an `AudioContext` — the same contract every shipped cue
   honours.

Why (rationale of record): the game is already rhythmic — every weapon fires on
the silent shared lattice — but the player cannot hear it. Locking music to that
lattice is the cheapest large step in perceived production value and tension,
and it makes the existing fire cadence read as deliberate mastery rather than a
technical detail.

### Additional acceptance criteria

- **AC-M1 — Tempo derived.** A test proves bar and phrase boundaries are
  computed from `beatBpm`, and that changing the tempo moves every boundary with
  it (no hard-coded period anywhere).
- **AC-M2 — Pure intensity, bar-aligned layers.** A test proves the intensity
  parameter is a pure function of the documented state inputs and that every
  layer transition occurs on a bar boundary; the same state sequence produces
  the same transition list.
- **AC-M3 — Mix and safe degradation.** A test proves music never exceeds its
  documented ceiling against the SFX contract, that the no-`AudioContext` path
  is silent and non-throwing, and that music volume is independent of SFX
  volume/mute.

The contract rows for each new state, layer and parameter must be added to the
traceability table owned by **Music contract mapping and traceability guard
(AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3)**.

# Ignore the eval harness validation output dir (experience-out/) in .gitignore

## Problem statement

`npm run validate-experience` writes `experience-out/experience-validation.json` and `experience-out/experience-validation.md` into the working tree, but `experience-out/` is not in `.gitignore`. As a result, validation artefacts can be swept into `git add -A` and committed — this already happened once in commit `8d948f7b` (branch `dev`).

## Users

- Agent developers running baseline captures and experience validation locally.
- The `implement.py finish` pipeline which runs `git add -A` and must not commit generated artefacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `.gitignore` lists `experience-out/` beside the existing `eval-output/` entry, with an explanatory comment referencing this work item.
2. `experience-out/experience-validation.json` and `experience-validation.md` are removed from tracking via `git rm --cached` (files remain on disk locally).
3. A fresh run of `npm run validate-experience -- eval-output/balance-report.json` produces output in `experience-out/` and leaves `git status --porcelain` clean.
4. `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` (or `docs/BALANCING.md`) states that the `experience-out/` output directory is git-ignored.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Impact

Operators running experience validation will no longer have local artefacts accidentally committed to the repository.

## Constraints

- Files must remain on disk after `git rm --cached` (local availability preserved).
- Entry must be placed in `.gitignore` alongside the existing `eval-output/` rule for consistency.
- Documentation update should be a single sentence — no deep spec change.

## Existing state

- `.gitignore` contains `eval-output/`, `recordings/`, `capture-output/`, `perf-output/` — all local-only artefact trees.
- `experience-out/` is missing from this list.
- Two files (`experience-validation.json`, `experience-validation.md`) are currently tracked in the repo.

## Desired change

1. Add `experience-out/` to `.gitignore` with a comment referencing this work item.
2. Untrack the two committed files: `git rm --cached experience-out/experience-validation.json experience-out/experience-validation.md`.
3. Add a one-line note in `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` that the output directory is git-ignored (or in `docs/BALANCING.md` if that is the more natural home).

## Key Files

- `.gitignore` — add the new entry
- `docs/EXPERIENCE_VALIDATION.md` — add git-ignore note
- `scripts/validate-experience.mjs` — reference only (to confirm output path)

## Related work

- **AH-0MVWAVJJG003S0XF** — Capture pre-change weapon balance baseline (parent/discovered-from; this item was found during that work).
- **AH-0MVSE1A7O002PXAO** — Journal the tune CSV edit (similar .gitignore + untrack pattern).
- **AH-0MU480XW8009160C** — Ignore the generated standups/ directory (precedent for .gitignore chore).

# Intake brief — evaluate-tune-progress watchdog test races on src/data tune journal

## Headline

Point the `evaluate-tune-progress` real-CLI test at a per-test temp data
root so its watchdog assertions never read the shared `src/data` directory,
removing the last concurrent-run race window.

## Problem statement

The `--watchdog` case in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` asserts on
state in the **real** `src/data` directory (the journal scan and the CSV
digest), so a sibling vitest worker that momentarily holds a journal there —
or edits the tracked CSV — can fail it spuriously. The observed flake
(`expected ['enemy-configs.csv.tune-journal'] to deeply equal []`) was
already mitigated once by scoping the journal assertion to the run's own pid
(commit `88e6827a`, AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS), but the test still reads the shared
directory, so AC1 of it ("the test no longer reads shared mutable state in
`src/data`") is not yet satisfied in letter and two narrow race windows
remain: an unparseable foreign journal counts as owned, and a sibling suite
doing a real-edit `--tune` spawn could transiently change the CSV between the
test's two digest reads.

## Users

As a **developer running the unit suite in parallel**, I want the
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog test to observe only its own run, so a
concurrent worker's transient journal (or edit) can never fail my build.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The CLI's `--tune` data root is overridable per run (a seam in
   `resolveTuneCsvPath()` in `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — e.g. an
   `EVAL_TUNE_DATA_ROOT` env override, or a `--tune-root <dir>` flag), so a
   test can point `--tune` at a temp directory holding a copy of
   `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` without touching the repo file.
2. The `--watchdog` cases in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` run the
   real CLI against that per-test temp root; the CSV digest check and
   `journalsOwnedBy(run.pid)` assertions scan the temp root only — no read or
   write of `REPO_ROOT/src/data` remains in those cases.
3. Two concurrent full-suite `npm test` runs leave `evaluate-tune-progress`
   green (the shared-`src/data` race is eliminated structurally, not
   probabilistically).
4. Every other `evaluate-tune-progress` assertion still holds: per-run
   progress lines, no `[tune]` leak into stdout, four artifacts written, and
   the off-by-default and bad-budget (exit 2) cases.
5. The seam cannot silently diverge from the sweep's config reads: a
   redirected data root combined with a **value-changing** `--set` emits a
   stderr warning that the edit targets the redirected root while the sweep
   reads the bundled config store, and the seam is documented in the CLI
   `--help`/docs as a test-isolation hook.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A developer running `npm test` in parallel no longer sees a spurious
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog failure caused by another suite's
transient `src/data/*.tune-journal`.

## Constraints

- **Behaviour parity (gym↔game):** this is a test-isolation change to the
  `--tune` verification harness, not gameplay; no production game behaviour
  changes.
- **No silent divergence:** the candidate sweep's config reads go through the
  bundled config store (`src/data/*.csv` via Vite `?raw`, e.g.
  `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`), so a data-root override that only redirects
  the edit/journal target must be a documented test-isolation seam with a
  warning on value-changing edits — not a path for real tuning runs to point
  at a different CSV.
- Existing tests only ever issue **byte-level no-op edits** (`boss.health=1`),
  so redirecting the edit target is behaviour-identical for the suite; the
  seam must keep that true.
- Keep the change minimal: only `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and
  the CLI seam; do **not** refactor `evaluate-failfast.test.ts` or
  `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` (producer decision, Q2) and do not
  entangle the product-level concurrency work in AH-0MW25VH540078FDK.
- Work must happen in the worktree created by `implement.py start` (never the
  main checkout) per project rules.

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: `CSV` is hard-coded to
  `resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'src/data/enemy-configs.csv')`; `csvDigest()` reads the
  real file; `journalsOwnedBy(pid)` does `readdirSync(join(REPO_ROOT,
  'src/data'))` and counts any journal whose recorded pid matches the spawned
  CLI, plus any unparseable journal (`catch { return true }`).
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (line ~428) hard-codes
  `resolvePath(import.meta.dirname, '..')` + `src/data` + `tuneFile`; there is
  no override today. `executeTune()` (line ~657) resolves the CSV, journals it
  before editing, and the `main()` reconcile (line ~804) restores stale
  journals for the resolved path.
- The observed flake predates the pid-scope fix; commit `88e6827a`
  (AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS) already scoped the journal assertion to the run's own
  pid, which is why reruns were green and the remaining gap is the letter of
  AC1 plus the two tight residual windows.

## Desired change

1. Add the data-root override to `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (env var preferred:
   zero public CLI surface, trivially injected via `cliSpawnEnv()` in
   `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts`; a `--tune-root <dir>` flag is the acceptable
   alternative and then needs `--help` + `evaluate.d.mts` + `docs/` sync).
2. In `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: create a per-test temp data
   root (`mkdtempSync`), copy the shipped `enemy-configs.csv` into it, spawn
   with the override, and point `csvDigest()` and `journalsOwnedBy()` at the
   temp root (parameterise the dir instead of `REPO_ROOT/src/data`).
3. Emit the stderr warning in `executeTune()` when an override is combined
   with an edit whose `changed` is true; document the seam.

## Key Files

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — add the data-root override to
  `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (and the stderr warning near `attempt` in
  `executeTune()`).
- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` — per-test temp data root; digest
  and journal assertions scoped to it; update the file-header comment.
- `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts` — inject the override env var per spawn.
- `scripts/evaluate.d.mts` — type the new option if a `--tune-root` flag is
  chosen.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` (crash-safe journal §) / `docs/EVALUATION.md` — document
  the test-isolation seam.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — referenced only
  to confirm the sweep read path (no change).

## Related work

- **AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS** (completed, `88e6827a`) — the pid-scoped
  `journalsOwnedBy` fix this item builds on; partial overlap, antecedent.
- **AH-0MVSE1OPF008G1SB** (completed) — per-run progress + `--watchdog`
  (parent of this test file).
- **AH-0MVSE1A7O002PXAO** (completed) — crash-safe tune CSV journal.
- **AH-0MW25VH540078FDK** (open) — serialise concurrent `--tune` runs on the
  same balance CSV (shared journal path); product-level, related, out of
  scope here.
- **AH-0MW0Q1DCZ006AUGP** (completed) — weapon catalogue CSV codec (the
  item that discovered this flake, `discovered-from:`).
- **AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7** (completed, epic) — data-driven weapon tuning.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the override is used only by tests, and existing test runs
  keep every edit a byte-level no-op, so no real tuning run is affected.
- **Risk:** a future test/run combines the override with a value-changing
  edit and silently tunes nothing → mitigated by the AC5 stderr warning and
  docs.
- **Risk (scope creep):** threading the override into the config store's
  `?raw` loads would make real edits honour the temp root but is far larger
  and touches production load paths — explicitly out of scope; the warning +
  docs approach is proportionate for a test-isolation seam.
- **Risk:** the CLI parses options from argv only today; an env override
  must be documented in the source and the file-header comment so future
  readers understand why the test no longer reads the repo dir.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (2026-11-13, asked by Map): "Scope: the pid-scope fix already closed the
  recorded flake; how should this item proceed? A) per-test temp data root
  (CLI seam) — recommended; B) close as already addressed; C) minimal
  hardening." — Answer (producer): **A**. Source: interactive reply on
  work item AH-0MW22FTXP004Z4G5 (comment AH-C0MWF28EGI0074O58). Research:
  verified `resolveTuneCsvPath()` hard-codes the repo data root and the
  config store reads CSVs via `?raw` imports, so a seam is required for A.
- Q2 (2026-11-13, asked by Map): "If A, also refactor
  `evaluate-failfast.test.ts` to a temp root, or only
  `evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`?" — Answer (producer): **only
  `evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`** (as recommended). Source: interactive
  reply. Constraint recorded above; failfast's edit discipline already holds
  and widening scope risks entangling AH-0MW25VH540078FDK.

# Goal

As a player, I want hulls to be able to grant **extra upgrade bays** (more equipment/loadout slots than the base hull) as a special-reward axis, so the special-mission reward space is not limited to more hit points.

Follow-on from the producer's answer to Q2 on **AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55** ("2. A — create a work item to add upgrade bays"): the special-missions item ships its first reward as a hull with extra hit points; the **upgrade-bay concept does not yet exist in the data model** (HullRunStats carries only startingLives + speedMultiplier; upgrades are armour/firepower/systems), so extending the run-stats/loadout model for upgrade bays is tracked separately here.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2).

## Scope

- Introduce an **upgrade-bay concept** to the hangar hull model: a hull authoring how many bays (equipment/loadout slots) it deploys with, resolved into the run loadout and persisted under the existing `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload.
- Futures a hull reward that grants **extra upgrade bays** rather than (or in addition to) extra hit points — the second special reward the design of record names.
- Must reuse the shipped deployment path (`PlayScene` + `src/scenes/core/`) and the pure hangar economy; no second run implementation (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity). Gym coverage `GymHangar`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hull definition can author an upgrade-bay count, and the resolved deployment/loadout honours it (shipped run, no divergent copy).
- The bay count is persisted under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload with field-presence migration (no new storage key).
- `GymHangar` exercises the bay/bay-resolution behaviour with the same code as the game.
- Tests pin the bay model, the loadout resolution and the persistence round-trip; full suite green.

## Context gathered (intake, 2026-11-14)

**Duplicate check:** `wl search` for "bay", "upgrade bay", "loadout", "slot" found no item whose ACs overlap this one — the closest items (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF six-slot cap, AH-0MVVJRRN10038VFR HUD six-slot budget, AH-0MVZ0GGW1004502H upgrade-count off-by-one, and the hangar-loadout items AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ / AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D / AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX) implement the shipped slot/loadout rules this item builds on; none is a duplicate. No overlapping completed item found.

**Potentially related docs:** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (post-MVP list, §"Post-MVP mitigation backlog" names "extra hit points or extra upgrade bays" → AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55); `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 (same backlog wording); `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (GymHangar parity rows).

**Potentially related work items:** AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55 (parent epic — special missions; Q2 = a shut upgrade bays out of scope into this item); AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE (shipped Build Candidate D parent); AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (deployments start with no extra weapons — empty loadout legal); AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX (loadout trimmed to the six-slot cap); AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF (six-slot cap model); AH-0MVVJRRN10038VFR (HUD six-slot budget).

**Model research (repo):** `HullRunStats` (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) carries only `startingLives` + `speedMultiplier`; the run's only equipment-slot concept is the shared six-slot pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`, `src/core/constants.ts`, consumed by `src/powerups/slots.ts` — drop draw, collection gate, hold-full choice, HUD rows, `capDropIdsToSlotPool`). The hangar loadout (`HangarLoadout` = `{ startingWeapons, modifiers }`, `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is currently uncapped; the deployment (`buildHangarDeployment` → `HangarWarDeployment`) carries the resolved hull stats forward to `PlayScene`; `applyHangarWarDeployment` trims starting weapons to the six-slot cap. No "upgrade bay" semantics exist anywhere — the term appears only in the design-of-record backlog wording.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (upgrade-bay semantics) — OPEN QUESTION (needs producer)

**Q1 asked:** The design of record names "extra upgrade bays" as a hull reward axis but never defines what a bay *is*. The run's only equipment-slot concept today is the shipped six-slot power-up/weapon pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`), and the hangar loadout (`startingWeapons`/`modifiers`) is uncapped. What does one extra upgrade bay grant in the run?
Options: (a) **one extra shared run loadout slot** — a bay hull deploys with a raised equipment cap (6 + N, e.g. 7–8) for that deployment; the shared slot accounting (`powerups/slots.ts`: drop draw, collection gate, choice, HUD, pre-grant trim) is parameterised by the deployment's bay count; (b) **one extra starting-weapon slot in the hangar loadout selector** — the bay count expands how many distinct starting weapons a deployment may be equipped with (the run still trims to the shared cap during play); (c) **one extra hangar modifier slot** — expands the active loadout's modifier capacity; (d) other.

**Recommended:** (a) — the run's shared slots are the game's actual equipment slots, so like extra hit points the reward is felt *inside* the run; (b)/(c) only widen the pre-deployment pick list and are bounded by the shipped cap in-run. Base bay count = 6 (the shipped `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`); a save/payload without the field reads as 6 (field-presence).

### Q2 (ship a bay hull now?) — OPEN QUESTION (needs producer)

**Q2 asked:** How far does this item go? Options: (a) **model + mechanics + one shipped catalogue bay hull** (e.g. `hull-4`, authoring a bay count, grantable via `resolveHexGrant` like `hull-3`) so the axis is exercised end-to-end by `GymHangar`; wiring the ring's special-mission rotation to *offer* it stays a follow-on; (b) **also wire the bay hull as the second special reward** in the shipped rotation/offer surface within this item; (c) **model + mechanics only** — the bay hull exists only as test/fixture data, the real reward hull decided at planning.

**Recommended:** (a) — AC1/AC3 demand the resolved deployment honour an authored bay count through the shipped run with no divergent copy, which needs at least one real authored bay hull to exercise; the rotation/offer surface belongs to the special-missions epic (AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55, already in review) and is a natural follow-on.

### Q3 (where the bay count is persisted) — OPEN QUESTION (needs producer)

**Q3 asked:** AC2 says the bay count is "persisted under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload with field-presence migration (no new storage key)". # Strengthen a hexes defence

Problem statement: A player who owns a hex has no way to spend their banked salvage to make the bot defending it stronger. This item adds an "Upgrade Defences" flow: select a held hex on the map, open a hangar-style upgrade screen targeting that hex's bot, and spend minerals/cores on hangar-catalogue upgrades that fit the bot's ship.

## Users (with user stories)

- **Player (primary).** "When I select a hex I own, I want to send upgrades to the bot defending it, so the salvage I earned strengthens a hold I care about."
- **Player, making a purchase.** "I want to buy upgrades with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar, and only those that fit into the bot's existing ship — an upgrade to a weapon it already carries, or a new weapon in an empty slot."
- **Player, after a tick.** "I want the upgrades to stay on the bot between sorties, and to be gone for good if the hex loses its defence, so spending salvage is a real commitment."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Selecting a **held** hex on the hex map surfaces an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; activating it opens the bot-upgrade screen for that hex's defender. An unheld hex offers no such action, and the read-only `GymHexWar` map render never offers it either.
- The bot-upgrade screen reuses the shared hangar-screen model/renderer pattern (game and `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` parity): it lists the hangar-catalogue entries (weapons, hulls and modifiers) and shows each one's fit verdict for the focused bot — **upgrade existing** (the bot already carries the weapon → raise its level), **add to empty slot** (a weapon kind the bot does not carry → offered **only** when the bot has a free permanent slot), **re-hull** (a hull entry), **train** (a modifier entry), or a disabled reason (slot pool full / unaffordable / ring-gated). No second, drifting copy of the fit rule exists.
- A purchase is paid for in minerals and/or cores from the fleet's banked salvage (the hangar wallet, `HangarState.bankedMinerals`/`bankedCores`), spends exactly the displayed price, and applies the upgrade to the bot's ship: a new weapon kind occupies one permanent slot at level 1, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps the bot's `hullId` (keeping the existing carried loadout), and a modifier entry applies its effect to the bot. The fleet's owned sets, active hull/loadout and the player's deployed ship are untouched by a bot purchase.
- Weapon upgrades follow a **per-level upgrade price** (Q9 = B): a separate, authored upgrade-price rule for raising an already-carried weapon's level, distinct from the catalogue entry's purchase price for a new kind; both are documented in one pricing table.
- The bot's defence rating reflects the sent upgrades through the **one** existing rating formula (`defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` mapping); a purchase returns a fresh payload with the defender's stored `defenceRating` recomputed and re-persisted, never a second derivation.
- Upgrade state persists on the `HexDefender` across between-sortie ticks and save/load round-trips (additive optional fields, field-presence migration, same pattern as `skills`), and is destroyed with the bot when its hex falls in a defence tick (existing `applyDefence` path — a fallen hex loses its defender).
- Tests cover: the fit rule (upgrade-existing vs add-to-empty-slot vs re-hull vs train vs disabled states), purchase economics (price, per-level upgrade price, wallet deduction, refused purchases), snapshot update + rating recompute, persistence round-trip and fall-destruction, corruption tolerance of the stored upgrade state, the map action surface and the gym parity assertion.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` for the new bot-upgrade control surface.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can now spend earned minerals and cores to send hangar upgrades — weapons, hulls and modifiers — to a bot defending a hex they own, and read the strengthened rating on the map; giving the hangar economy a second, defence-shaped sink.

## Constraints

- **Pure and injectable:** the fit rule, purchase application and rating recompute live in the pure core (hangar economy / a new `botUpgrade` module), no Phaser, no storage access; scenes only present and persist.
- **Same-data-model rule (producer Q2):** the bot uses the same ship data model as a player-controlled ship — the permanent slot model (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` = 6 shared weapon/power-up slots) and the victory-snapshot vocabulary from `AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ` (`DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`: permanent weapon levels, power-up levels, consumable pools). The bot is never flown; its loadout is stored data that feeds the one rating formula.
- **Hangar catalogue entries (producer Q3):** the upgrade pool is the shipped `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` — **weapons, hulls and modifiers** (producer Q10 = "everything") — no new economy, no new currency; ring gating and prices reused as authored, plus the new per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).
- **Slot-fit rule (producer Q8 = A):** a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an empty permanent slot; a weapon the bot already carries is always offered as a level-upgrade. Hulls and modifiers have no slot requirement (a hull swaps `hullId`, a modifier applies its effect).
- **One interaction (producer Q4):** an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action in the hex summary section opens a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (the hangar screen) scoped to the bot — same screen pattern, different purchase target.
- **Destruction (producer Q5):** upgrades are persistent **unless** the hex loses a defence tick, which destroys the bot (today's `applyDefence` already unholds the hex and drops its defender; nothing new to build there).
- **Rating (producer Q6):** upgrades change the stored `defenceRating`, recomputed through the single shipped formula.
- **No player-ship effect (producer Q7):** a bot purchase never touches the player's deployed ship, active loadout or the fleet's owned sets.
- **No schema version bump:** new optional fields read by field presence, matching `skills` / `frontierTick`.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `HexDefender` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is a derived-rating record — `hullId`, `defenceRating`, `bankedMinerals`, optional `skills` — with no weapon slots or upgrade levels. It is never flown; every defence is arithmetic over stored numbers.
- The sibling item (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ) lands the bot ship-model vocabulary in the economy: `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`, `UPGRADE_STAT_BUCKETS` (one frozen row per `WeaponId`/`PowerUpId`), `defenderStatBuckets`, `snapshotDefenderUpgrades`, and `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` — already merged (commits `46d217b5`, `58dc8edc`). Its capture-cycle threading is being delivered through its own child items (e.g. AH-0MWHF6ZHW0058SMX); **this item depends on that snapshot existing on `HexDefender`** (dependency edge recorded).
- The player-ship slot model is the permanent six-slot pool shared by weapons and power-ups (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` in `src/core/constants.ts`, `capDropIdsToSlotPool` in `src/powerups/slots.ts`).
- The hangar economy (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) owns prices, `canBuy`/`buy`, `purchaseWeight`, ring gating and `resolvePlayerStrength`; the catalogue (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) holds hulls, starting weapons and modifiers with two-currency prices.
- The hangar screen (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) is the pure model + one renderer used by the shipped hangar scene **and** `GymHangar`; the hex map (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` + `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) renders focused-hex intel in the right-hand detail panel, with held hexes selectable but not actionable.
- Defence ticks (`runFrontierTick` → `applyDefence`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) already destroy a fallen hex's defender (`held=false`, `defender=null`).

## Desired change

1. **Bot ship model.** `HexDefender` carries the shipped upgrade-snapshot vocabulary (permanent weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) as additive optional fields, alongside the existing hull/rating/skills — the same-data-model rule (Q2). The bot's slot occupancy derives from the stored levels against `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`.
2. **Fit rule (pure).** A new pure function answers, per catalogue entry and per defender: `upgrade-existing` (bot already carries the weapon → level +1), `add-to-empty-slot` (new weapon kind, **only when a free slot exists**), `re-hull` (hull entry, no slot requirement), `train` (modifier entry, no slot requirement), or a disabled reason (slot pool full, unaffordable in either currency, ring-gated). The fit rule and the hangar's `canBuy` combine into one verdict per row.
3. **Per-level weapon-upgrade price (Q9 = B).** One authored table defines the upgrade price for raising an already-carried weapon's level (distinct from the catalogue's new-kind purchase price). Both prices appear on the row and are paid from the hangar wallet.
4. **Purchase application (pure).** Spending the displayed price applies the upgrade to the defender's ship: a new weapon kind enters at level 1 in one permanent slot, an already-carried weapon rises one level, a hull entry swaps `hullId` keeping the carried loadout, a modifier entry applies its effect; `defenceRating` recomputes through `defenderRatingFromSnapshot` / the buckets mapping — one formula (Q6). A refused purchase returns the payload unchanged.
5. **Map action.** The held-hex detail panel (the "hex summary section") gains an `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action; `HexMapScene` wires it to open the bot-upgrade screen for the focused defender (Q4). Unheld hexes offer nothing; the gym's read-only render (no handlers) offers nothing — parity by construction.
6. **Bot-upgrade screen.** A hangar-screen-style scene scoped to one defender: same pure model + one renderer shape as `hangarScreen`, showing the fit verdicts, both price kinds and the bot's current loadout/rating; purchases return a fresh payload that the scene persists. Game and gym (if exercised) share the model/renderer so they cannot drift.
7. **Persistence and destruction.** Purchases persist via the versioned store (additive optional fields, field-presence parse). A defence-tick fall destroys the bot including its upgrades through the existing `applyDefence` path (Q5).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HexDefender` gains additive optional upgrade-snapshot fields (weapon/power-up levels, consumable pools) mirroring `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/botUpgrade.ts` (new) — the pure fit rule, the per-level upgrade-price table (Q9 = B), purchase application and per-row verdict for a defender's upgrade options (own module so the scenes never derive a fit).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — any shared helper the purchase needs (wallet spend, snapshot → rating via existing `defenderRatingFromSnapshot`).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parse/round-trip of the new optional fields (field presence).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the held-hex `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action row + activation wiring in the detail panel.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — handler wiring (`onUpgradeDefences(hexId)` → open the bot-upgrade screen) and the route back after a purchase.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScreen.ts` (new) + `src/scenes/hangarWar/botUpgradeScene.ts` (or a mode of the existing hangar screen) — the pure model + one renderer for the bot-upgrade screen.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` (and `GymHangar` if it renders the upgrade screen) — parity/no handlers for the new surface.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, README — the new control surface and its parity entry.

## Related work

- **Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades (AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ)** — dependency: supplies the `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` model, the stat-bucket mapping and the snapshot-aware rating this item's purchases consume; its capture-cycle threading first puts the snapshot on `HexDefender`.
- Hangar economy and unlock tree (AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6) — owns `canBuy`/`buy`, prices and ring gating the purchase path reuses.
- Capture cycle — hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6) — the module that creates `HexDefender`s.
- Hex-map intel / map screen (AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2) — the detail panel that gains the `UPGRADE DEFENCES` action.
- Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with special skills (AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1) — precedent for additive optional defender fields and the skills pattern (modifier `train` applies here).
- Versioned `ai_hell_hangar_war` store with migration (AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV) — the back-compat pattern new optional fields follow.
- Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP) — the tick path that destroys a fallen bot (Q5).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk (highest):** spendable upgrades let a player push a held hex's rating high, making well-defended hexes mathematically unretakeable — the same accepted consequence as the sibling item's Q3 = A. *Mitigation:* one rating formula and one mapping table, so a follow-up tuning item can cap or rescale prices without touching saves; measure from real runs before filing.
- **Pricing granularity risk (Q9 = B):** the per-level weapon-upgrade price is new authored data; its exact progression is a balance knob. *Mitigation:* one documented table in `botUpgrade.ts`, authorable without code changes; defaults chosen conservatively at implement time and reviewed in the effort/risk notes.
- **Dependency risk:** the brief assumes the sibling's snapshot-on-`HexDefender` threading lands first. If it slips, this item's data model cannot build. *Mitigation:* dependency edge recorded; implement after the sibling's capture threading.
- **Save-compatibility risk:** new optional fields must be omitted when empty and parsed defensively, or existing saves/fixtures drift. *Mitigation:* the `skills` pattern exactly; store round-trip + pre-change-save tests.
- **Wallet-conflict risk:** bot purchases spend the same banked minerals/cores the player uses for fleet unlocks — a bot spend can starve the hangar. *Deliberate per Q3/Q8 (A):* catalogue-priced, shared wallet; documented rather than gated in this item.
- **Modifier-fit risk (Q10 = everything):** a modifier whose effect targets run stats (e.g. `extra-lives`) has no bot meaning; only modifier effects with a stored-bot effect (e.g. `defence-skill`) can be sent. *Mitigation:* the fit rule classifies modifier effects by whether they change stored defender data; `extra-lives`-style effects are shown disabled with a reason rather than silently charged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** candidates deliberately excluded — a bot that is actually flown in combat, any new currency, new catalogue entries, and any change to player-ship progression or the frontier tuning constants. Each excluded candidate must become its own work item rather than growing this one.
- **Assumption (Q8, A):** the upgrade screen offers every catalogue entry the fleet can afford (ring + wallet gating), subject to the slot-fit rule for new weapons; a purchase spends banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — the bot gets the entry, the fleet does not.
- **Assumption (Q9, B):** a per-level upgrade-price table governs raising an already-carried weapon's level; a new weapon kind pays the catalogue purchase price and enters at level 1, occupying one permanent slot when one is free.
- **Assumption:** "permanent slots" for the bot mean the shared six-slot weapon/power-up pool (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`), counted by distinct permanently-carried kinds — the bot's stored data, never a live battle.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What does 'send upgrades for the ship' mean?" — **Answer (operator):** upgrade the **defending bot** (the bot left in the hex). *Source:* interactive reply.
- Q2 — "Does the bot get its own slot system?" — **Answer (operator):** the bot should be the **same as a player-controlled ship**, using the same data model so it has **slots etc.** *Research:* `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (six shared weapon/power-up slots) and the sibling item's `DefenderUpgradeSnapshot` are the vocabularies this maps onto.
- Q3 — "What counts as an upgrade the player can send?" — **Answer (operator):** **hangar catalogue entries**, purchased with minerals and/or cores from the Hangar. *Research:* `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` + `canBuy`/`buy` already implement two-currency, ring-gated purchases.
- Q4 — "What's the UI interaction?" — **Answer (operator):** add an **"upgrade defenses" button to the hex summary section**, which opens **a version of the player-ship upgrade scene (hangar)** but upgrades the bot instead of the player's ship.
- Q5 — "Persistence and limits?" — **Answer (operator):** **persistent unless it loses a defence tick, in which case it is destroyed** (matches today's `applyDefence`: a fallen hex unholds and drops its defender).
- Q6 — "How does the upgrade affect the bot's defence?" — **Answer (operator):** it **changes the defence rating** (recomputed through the one shipped formula).
- Q7 — "Does sending upgrades affect the player's ship?" — **Answer (operator):** **no**.
- Q8 — "Which catalogue entries can the player send?" — **Answer (operator):** **A** — every catalogue entry the fleet can afford, spending banked salvage without granting the fleet an unlock — **refined**: a weapon the bot does **not** already own is offered **only** when the bot has an **empty slot**. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q9 — "How does 'upgrade to an existing weapon' price?" — **Answer (operator):** **B** — a **separate per-level upgrade price** (its own authored pricing table), distinct from the catalogue purchase price for a new kind. *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).
- Q10 — "Which catalogue kinds are in scope?" — **Answer (operator):** **everything** — weapons, hulls and modifiers are all sendable (each with its own fit rule; hulls re-hull, modifiers apply their stored effect). *Source:* interactive reply (round 2).

# Test runner crashes with UnboundLocalError when a full-scope suite resolves to no commands

## Problem Statement

`run_tests.py` crashes with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_changed_flag'` when a named suite resolves to zero commands. Instead of reporting the empty resolution gracefully, the function references a variable that was never bound.

## Users

- Agent sessions that run the test skill with a named suite (e.g. `--suite node`) that happens to resolve to no commands in the current repo.
- CI / automation that invokes the test runner with varying suites across repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-scope run whose suite resolves to no commands completes without an `UnboundLocalError` — either with an actionable message naming the suite and resolution path, or a clean early return with a zero-command report.
2. The `state_changed_flag` variable is initialised before the command-execution loop (or the loop body guard handles the empty case), so the post-loop aggregation path never touches an unbound variable.
3. A regression test exercises the zero-command path (mocking `commands` to an empty list, or using a suite name that resolves to nothing) and asserts no crash.

## Impact

Users running the test runner against a suite with zero commands get a clear, actionable error message instead of an obscure Python `UnboundLocalError` crash.

## Constraints

- Fix is in a shared skill (`run_tests.py` in the `test` skill scripts); changes must not break existing callers.
- The existing `state_changed_flag` semantics (mid-run checkout movement tracking) must be preserved for the normal non-empty command path.

## Existing State

`run_tests.py` initialises `state_changed_flag` inside the `for cmd in commands:` loop body (line 3188). After the loop, the function reads `state_changed_flag` on line 3281 to populate `state_changed_during_run` in the result dict. When `commands` is empty, the loop body never executes, leaving the name unbound.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Move `state_changed_flag` initialisation before the `for cmd in commands:` loop (line ~3183, after `slot_waits`).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/tests/` — Add regression test for the zero-command path.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The fix is narrowly scoped to the `UnboundLocalError`. Do not refactor other loop-scoped variables (e.g. `command_waits`, `command_elapsed`) unless they show the same pattern.
- **Assumption:** Moving the initialisation before the loop is safe — `state_changed_flag` is reset per-command inside the loop for the normal case. We should verify whether a per-iteration reset is actually needed or whether a single pre-loop initialisation suffices.
- **Risk:** If `state_changed_flag` is intentionally per-command (reset for each iteration), a single pre-loop initialisation may lose the reset semantics. The fix should preserve per-command reset only if the logic requires it; otherwise the pre-loop init is sufficient.

## Related Work

- Discovered from AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 ("Bot oscillates too much") — the agent was running the test skill during implementation and hit this crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Does `state_changed_flag` need per-command reset, or is a single pre-loop initialisation sufficient?" — Answer (Map): A pre-loop initialisation to `None` is sufficient. The per-command reassignment on line 3224 (`state_changed_flag = run.get("state_changed_during_run")`) overwrites the value each iteration; the post-loop read (line 3281) captures the last iteration's value (or `None` if zero iterations). The bug is simply that the declaration line never runs when the loop body is skipped.

# Procedurally generated Hex Map

## Problem statement

The hex ring's **shape** is already generated at runtime from the shared `6 × n`
geometry, but its **content** — boss identity, strengths/weaknesses, the granted
weapon or upgrade, base aggression and the optional variety axes — is
hand-authored data for rings 1 and 2 only, so the war stops where that table
ends. The producer has decided that **every ring should be procedurally
generated from the war's seeded RNG**: the same `(seed, ringIndex)` always yields
the same ring, and the frontier has no authored ceiling.

## Users

- **Player** — "Every war's map is generated from its seed, the frontier never
  stops at ring 2, and the same seed replays the same map."
- **Designer** — "I no longer author a table per ring, and the generator honours
  the shipped ring rules so procedural rings stay balanced and readable."
- **Test/agent** — "The generated ring is a pure function of `(seed, ringIndex)`,
  so I can assert determinism and run it headlessly in the gym with game
  parity."

## Producer decisions (recorded this intake)

- **Q1 = B — all rings procedural.** Rings 1 and 2 are generated from the seed
  like every other ring; `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the CSV seeds are retired as
  the runtime content source.
- **Q2 = A — pure function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on
  demand.** Only the existing `HexState` is persisted; stored rings are never
  regenerated.
- **Q3 = A — cycle real catalogue grants with level scaling.** Larger rings
  repeat catalogue entries and each repeat raises an upgrade/weapon level
  (capped).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated ring content is a **pure, deterministic function of
  `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`**: the same seed/ring yields identical hexes (ids,
  coordinates, boss, strengths/weaknesses, grant, base aggression and variety
  axes), and at least two distinct seeds yield materially different rings.
- The authored runtime table `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the `hex-ring-1.csv` /
  `hex-ring-2.csv` seeds are **retired as the runtime content source** (no scene
  or runtime path imports authored ring content; the CSV parity test is removed
  or replaced), and rings 1 and 2 generate from the seed like every other ring.
- Every generated ring satisfies the shipped design invariants, validated
  loudly rather than repaired: exactly one weapon hex and it is the ring's
  hardest, one special-mission hex granting a hull, at least one beatable hex,
  unique ids and coordinates, and the aggression band/budget rules.
- **Grant economy:** the generator prefers unowned catalogue entries; when a
  ring exhausts them it cycles level-capable entries and each repeat raises the
  weapon/power-up level (capped at `MAX_LEVEL`), while unlevellable repeats
  (hull/modifier) bank a mineral payout; every granted hex resolves to a real
  effect (never a silent no-op).
- **Existing saves remain playable and unchanged**: a stored ring (full or
  partial) is never regenerated or discarded; a fresh/empty ring generates from
  the seed; defensive parse and migration behaviour is covered by tests.
- Unit, property and integration tests cover determinism, distinct-seed
  variety, invariant enforcement across many seeds and large ring indices, the
  grant-economy rule, and the save/load round-trip; `GymHexWar` renders the same
  generated model as the game.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can push the frontier indefinitely: every war's hex map is generated
from its seed rather than stopping where hand-authored content ends.

## Constraints

- **One seeded stream.** Generation draws from the shipped seeded RNG
  (`createSeededRng` / `createHangarWarRng`, `normaliseSeed`) — no `Math.random`
  in content decisions. Draws must be derived per `(seed, ringIndex)` (and per
  hex) so a change in one ring cannot shift another ring's map.
- **Pure and headless.** The generator lives in the pure core
  (`src/core/hangarWar/`) with no Phaser, storage or scene dependency, so the
  map scene and `GymHexWar` share exactly one code path (gym↔game parity).
- **Preserve the published map.** The known-ahead intel promise (boss,
  strengths/weaknesses, aggression, grant) and the `6 × n` shape are unchanged;
  only *where content comes from* changes.
- **Finite grant vocabulary.** The hangar catalogue holds roughly 12–14 entries
  (hulls, weapons, modifiers, defence-skill), while ring 3 needs 18 distinct
  grants and ring *n* needs `6 × n` — so the level-scaling repeat rule (Q3 = A)
  is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
- **Deterministic identity.** Generated boss identities and hex ids must be
  stable for a seed and traceable in telemetry; hex ids must stay unique within
  the ring and stable across reloads.
- **No new combat implementations.** Personalities resolve through the existing
  bounded vocabularies (`HEX_PERSONALITY_IDS`, `HEX_LANDMARK_IDS`) and shared
  mechanics; generation only assigns them (at most one weapon hex and one
  special mission per ring).
- Aggression stays a whole number in `[0, 9]`; the frontier budget and
  beatable-hex invariants are preserved.

## Existing state

- **Shape generated, content authored.** `ringCoordinates` / `ringSize` compute
  the `6 × n` geometry; `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`)
  authors rings 1 (6 hexes) and 2 (12 hexes). `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv`
  mirror that table and a parity test fails if they drift.
- **No shipped ring 3.** The only ring-3 content is test fixture data
  (`VARIETY_RING_DEFINITIONS` in
  `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`); `aggressionScenarios.ts`
  already synthesises a deterministic placeholder shape for "ring 3+" in the
  harness — precedent, not shipping code.
- **Materialisation** goes through `materialiseRing` / `openNextRing`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`), which call `createRingState` and leave
  the ring unchanged when an authored successor is missing, so a war stalls at
  the last authored ring.
- **Seeded RNG and seed plumbing exist.** The payload carries a normalised
  `seed` (set from the run seed when a war starts); `createHangarWarRng` exposes
  `next`/`nextInt`/`pick` over the shipped mulberry32 stream, and
  `specialRotationSeed` demonstrates per-index stream mixing.
- **Precedent for generation modes.** AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT shipped per-wave
  `curve` / `fixed` / `dynamic` modes (`dynamic` = regenerated at runtime, seeded
  from the run RNG, reproducible per seed) — the project already has the
  vocabulary for seeded content.
- **The original intake premise was half right:** geometry is runtime-generated,
  content was build-time authored data.

## Desired change

Replace the authored ring-content source with a seeded generator used by **all**
rings. The generator produces a complete, valid `HexRingDefinition`-shaped ring
for any ring index from `(seed, ringIndex)` using the shared RNG and the shipped
catalogues/vocabularies, and flows through the existing materialisation, intel,
map and capture seams. Definition lookup by hex id must be derivable from the
same seed, and repeated catalogue grants must level up rather than no-op.

## **Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — add the seeded ring-content generator; keep
  `validateRingDefinitions` / `generateRing` pure and reuse them.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` — add a per-ring/per-hex derived stream (mirroring
  `specialRotationSeed`); do not add a second generator.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — retire the authored runtime table; keep only
  catalogue/vocabulary exports the generator draws from.
- `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`,
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — retire the seed/parity pair.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing` / `openNextRing` and
  grant application (`withGrantedEntry`) generate on demand and apply the
  level-scaling repeat rule.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/specialMission.ts` —
  definition lookup by id and the default definitions source consult the
  generator.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts`, `hexDifficulty.ts`, `hexDefence.ts` — the
  profile, aggression band and budget rules the generator must satisfy.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts` — the grant pool and the
  level caps (`MAX_LEVEL`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — remove the
  authored default and verify one rendered code path.
- Fixtures/tests: `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`,
  `aggressionScenarios.ts`, `hexVarietyDocs.test.ts`, gym/doc parity tests.
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and module comments.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** — Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions
  (completed). Origin of `hexRing.ts`, `validateRingDefinitions` and the authored
  rings; its producer decision chose authored content, which this item now
  reverses by producer decision (Q1 = B).
- **AH-0MUJSUQD8003FSUT** — Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed,
  hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration (completed). Closest
  precedent: a `dynamic` mode regenerated at runtime from the run RNG,
  reproducible per seed.
- **AH-0MWEW4ANW009GGX7** — Hex variety data vocabulary, fixtures and loud
  validation (completed). Defines the personality/contract/landmark vocabularies
  the generator assigns.
- **AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P** — HexMap aggression increases too quickly (completed).
  The aggression budget/band rules procedural rings must honour.
- **AH-0MWJ51KUS005WQK6**, **AH-0MWF0CTQB001XFE1** — special-mission hexes;
  **AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH** — ring landmarks. The invariants the generator must
  preserve.
- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB** — Held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action (blocked,
  tangential): consumes the map read model; generated rings must not regress it.
- **AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5** — Rebalance ring 2's grind budget (open, tangential):
  generated aggression must not reintroduce the grind problem it tracks.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Blast radius (main risk).** Retiring the authored table and CSV seeds reaches
  many tests, fixtures, scenes and docs that import `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`.
  Planning should decompose this as an epic into: generator, retirement/migration,
  definition-lookup wiring, grant level-scaling, save compatibility, and
  tests/docs.
- **Determinism contract.** Adding a field or changing a draw order changes every
  seed's map. Treat the draw sequence as a versioned contract and pin it with
  golden tests; scope generation to the pure `(seed, ringIndex)` inputs.
- **Tutorial variance.** Ring 1 is now seed-dependent: every war opens on a
  different ring. If the first war must stay a fixed tutorial, that is a separate
  decision; this brief assumes the producer's all-procedural choice stands.
- **Grant-economy detail.** Q3 = A did not specify repeats of entries with no
  level dimension (hull/modifier). Assumption: prefer unowned entries, level up
  level-capable repeats to `MAX_LEVEL`, and bank a mineral payout for
  unlevellable repeats (reusing the shipped banking rule). Confirm or correct.
- **Validation cost.** Decide whether generated rings are validated on every
  materialisation, only in tests/CI, or once per ring open.
- **Save compatibility.** A stored ring must never be regenerated or lost; an
  old/absent payload must parse defensively. Add a migration test.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Turning this into a new-boss / new-mechanic content suite
  would balloon it. Extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items, not
  folded into this one.

## Open questions

None outstanding — Q1–Q3 are answered. The documented assumptions above (grant
repeats for hulls/modifiers, tutorial variance, validation cadence) are recorded
so the producer can correct them without blocking the plan.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which rings become procedural, and does the authored content stay?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B — all rings procedural**, including
  rings 1–2; retire `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the CSV seeds and regenerate
  rings 1–2 from a seed too. Evidence: options recorded in comment
  `AH-C0MWLAGDNN006KLTX`; research inspected
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, `src/data/hex-ring-*.csv` and
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`.
- **Q2 — How is a generated ring reproduced and stored?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — pure function of
  `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on demand**; persist only the existing
  `HexState`, no schema migration. Evidence: comment `AH-C0MWLAGECE008CFOM`;
  research inspected `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (`materialiseRing`),
  `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` (`HangarWarPayload.seed`) and
  `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`.
- **Q3 — How should generated rings source grants once the catalogue runs out?**
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — cycle real catalogue grants with
  level scaling**; repeats raise an upgrade/weapon level (capped). Evidence:
  comment `AH-C0MWLAGEWP002U2ZA`; research counted ~12–14 catalogue entries in
  `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` against ring 3's 18 required grants, and
  confirmed `withGrantedEntry` currently only adds an owned id (no level raise).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** – Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions (completed)
- **AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** – Author shipped hex variety content on ring 1 (one landmark and one contract) (completed)
- **AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0** – Rush push into the next ring is playable (AC8 gap) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, 0mwfdqcfv007bze5, 0mwj51kus005wqk6, absent, acceptance (+453 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, 0mwfdqcfv007bze5, 0mwj51kus005wqk6, absent, acceptance (+428 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mujsuqd8003fsut, absent, acceptance, action, add (+357 more)
