# Speed Up power-up affects weapons only

## Problem statement

The Speed Boost (P5) power-up currently increases **both** the ship's movement speed (thrust and max speed) and its rate of fire by 50 % for 10 seconds. Design intent has changed: Speed Boost should be a **weapons-only** power-up — it must increase rate of fire but leave ship movement untouched. Today an active Speed Boost makes the ship harder to control (faster drift/top speed), which is not the intended effect.

## Users

- **Player** — when collecting a Speed Boost (P5), expects faster firing for the duration, with the ship handling exactly as normal.
  - *"As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost I want my weapons to fire faster, but my ship to handle exactly as it does without the power-up."*
- **Game designer / producer** — expects the GDD, power-up descriptions and README to describe P5 as a fire-rate boost only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — With P5 active, the player ship's **movement is unchanged**: thrust and max speed equal the un-boosted values in the playable game (`PlayScene`) and in every gym. `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` and `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` no longer exist (removed, not left returning 1).
- **AC2** — With P5 active, the player's **rate of fire still increases by 50 %** (effective 1.5 × fire rate) for the level-resolved duration, applied live every frame through the single shared `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer` step (so the game and all gyms inherit it); re-collect refreshes the full duration (never additive), expiry returns the rate to normal, and the boost survives respawn.
- **AC3** — `EffectsRegistry.fireRateMultiplier()` is the **single authority** for the P5 multiplier, reading the level-resolved catalogue stat directly (it no longer delegates to a removed movement accessor); the multiplier value and duration are unchanged.
- **AC4** — **Documentation updated:** the GDD P5 row says the Speed Boost increases **rate of fire** (not movement), and the `types.ts` description, `effects.ts`/`powerUpLevels.ts` doc comments/labels, README references and gym doc comments are updated to match. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship skill release pipeline.)
- **AC5** — **Test cleanup and coverage:** existing tests that assert the P5 movement boost are removed/renamed (not silently left asserting removed behaviour); the fire-rate assertions are retained and strengthened; a regression test proves movement (thrust/max speed) is identical with P5 active while fire rate is boosted; parity/equivalence tests are updated to the new API.
- **AC6** — **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Speed Boost becomes a clean weapons-only power-up: players get faster fire without the ship suddenly handling differently, so the effect is predictable and no longer punishes movement control.

## Constraints

- P5 duration (level-resolved 10 s → 20 s) and multiplier value (1.5 × at level 0, cap 2.5 ×) must not change; only the movement axis is removed.
- The registry module must stay engine-agnostic (no Phaser imports).
- Gym parity principle: the game and every gym consume the same shared `_tickPlayer` step, so the change must not fork gym behaviour (`AGENTS.md` gym-parity rule).
- Hull run-stat speed scaling (`scaleShipConfigForHull`) is **not** part of P5 and must keep working — those deployments scale the base ship config, not `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- No new balance config value is needed.

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) returns the level-resolved `speed_boost` `speedMultiplier` stat (1.5 at level 0) while active, else 1.
- `EffectsRegistry.fireRateMultiplier()` currently simply returns `this.speedMultiplier()`.
- `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) applies both each frame:
  `player.setSpeedMultiplier(registry.speedMultiplier()); player.setFireRateMultiplier(registry.fireRateMultiplier());`
- `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (`src/entities/Player.ts`) stores `_speedMultiplier` and re-derives `_config` from `_baseConfig` via `_applySpeedMultiplier()`. It is called only from `_tickPlayer` (plus `setConfig` calls `_applySpeedMultiplier`).
- Hull speed scaling uses `scaleShipConfigForHull` (`src/core/hangarWar/hullSpeed.ts`), applied to the base `ShipConfig` at deployment — it does **not** call `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- P5 is documented as movement + fire rate in: GDD §4.4 P5 row (`docs/Game Design Document.md` line ~1266), `src/powerups/types.ts` `speed_boost.description`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` label/rationale, `src/powerups/effects.ts` module doc, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` module doc, README (shared combat core, effects registry, gym entries), and `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` doc.
- Tests asserting the removed movement accessor (`EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()`): `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` (the `speed_boost: (r) => r.speedMultiplier()` probe map). Fire-rate-only assertions that must be kept and strengthened (they already call `fireRateMultiplier()`, so they need no accessor change): `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`. No test calls `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` directly (verified repo-wide), so no test needs updating for that removal.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` and make `fireRateMultiplier()` read `stats('speed_boost').speedMultiplier ?? 1` directly while `speed_boost` is active (still a single authority for the fire-rate axis).
2. **Remove** the `player.setSpeedMultiplier(registry.speedMultiplier())` call from `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer`, leaving only `setFireRateMultiplier(...)`.
3. **Remove** `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (and its now-dead `_speedMultiplier` / `_applySpeedMultiplier` support), folding the plain config assignment into `setConfig`; update the `Player._baseConfig` doc comment.
4. **Update docs/descriptions:** GDD P5 row, `types.ts` description, `powerUpLevels.ts` label/description/rationale, `effects.ts` module/roadmap comments, README references, `GymPowerUpsUtility`/`GymPlayer`/`hullSpeed`/`hangarDeployment` doc comments — all to describe P5 as a fire-rate (weapons-only) boost.
5. **Clean up tests:** delete/replace movement-boost assertions; keep and strengthen fire-rate assertions; add a regression test that movement (thrust/max speed) is identical with P5 active while fire rate is 1.5 ×.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — remove `speedMultiplier()`; have `fireRateMultiplier()` read the catalogue stat directly; update module doc.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — remove the `setSpeedMultiplier(...)` call from `_tickPlayer`; update the step doc/comment.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — remove `setSpeedMultiplier()` and its dead `_speedMultiplier`/`_applySpeedMultiplier` support; simplify `setConfig`; update `_baseConfig` doc.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — change `speed_boost.description` to a rate-of-fire-only description.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — update the `speed_boost` `speedMultiplier` spec label/description/rationale to fire-rate wording.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the P5 row and related references.
- `README.md` — update shared-core / effects-registry / gym references that mention movement + fire rate.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — update the module doc (Speed Boost bullet + `setSpeedMultiplier` reference).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — update the "live Speed Boost multipliers" doc wording.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hullSpeed.ts` — update the doc comment that references `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — update the doc comment that references `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB** — "Speed power up should increase all speeds" (completed, shipped v0.1.6). This item **reverses** its movement-axis half: it added "all speeds" (movement + rate of fire); the new intent keeps only the weapon rate-of-fire half.
- **AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7** — "PlayScene: apply P5 Speed Boost multiplier live" (completed). Added the original movement-only application; its movement half is now retired.
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** — "Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)" (completed). Catalogue/effects foundation.
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ** — "Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math" (completed). Test foundation to be cleaned up.
- **AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC** — "Temporary upgrades should always be temporary" (completed). Preserves re-collect/expiry semantics referenced by AC2.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S** – Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement (completed)
- **AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V** – Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship (completed)
- **AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB** – Speed power up should increase all speeds (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: change, movement, powerup, ship, speed (+2 more)
- `README.md` — matched: change, movement, powerup, ship, speed (+2 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: affects, change, movement, powerup, ship (+2 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "weapons only" could be read to add other weapon effects (bullet speed, damage). Scope is bounded to **removing the movement-speed axis and keeping the existing fire-rate boost**; anything wider becomes a linked follow-up, not scope here.
- **API removal risk:** removing `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` / `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` is a breaking internal API change. Mitigation: repo-wide search shows the only production caller is `_tickPlayer`; tests and doc comments are updated in the same change. `scaleShipConfigForHull` (hull run-stats) is independent and unaffected.
- **Misleading catalogue field name:** the level model stat is still called `speedMultiplier`. Renaming it to `fireRateMultiplier` would touch the power-up level specs, HUD and many tests; this item updates its user-facing label/description instead and leaves an internal rename to a potential follow-up.
- **Gym divergence risk:** gyms inherit `_tickPlayer`, so the removal must be made there only (never duplicated per-scene). Parity/equivalence tests are updated to guard this.
- **Assumption:** "Speed Up" in the item title refers to the existing **Speed Boost (P5)** power-up (no separate "Speed Up" power-up exists in the codebase).
- **Respawn interaction:** the multiplier must keep being re-applied each frame (fire-rate only) so it survives respawn and expiry — covered by AC2/AC5.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What is `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()`?** — Answer (Map, research): It is the `effects.ts` method returning the Speed Boost (P5) movement-speed multiplier (level-resolved `speedMultiplier` stat, 1.5 at level 0, else 1). It feeds `Player.setSpeedMultiplier(...)` in `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer`; `fireRateMultiplier()` currently delegates to it. Source: `src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`.
- **Q2: Should `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` be removed or kept?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"remove"*. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Should `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` be removed?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"remove"*. Research: only `_tickPlayer` calls it; hull speed uses `scaleShipConfigForHull`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4: Should the GDD / descriptions / README be updated?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"yes"*. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5: Should the existing movement-boost tests be updated?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"cleanup"*. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake brief — Modal Dialog to display Hex Combat results

## Problem statement

Returning to the hex map after a hex deployment currently reduces the whole
sortie to a single thin line (`RUN: VICTORY · score 1200`) plus a banked
win-bonus line, and on defeat it shows only `RUN: DEFEAT` with no explanation of
why the hex was not taken. The player cannot see, in one place, what the battle
outcome was, which rewards (salvage, granted weapon/upgrade, special reward,
contract/cache bonus) were actually paid, or — on a loss — what the defending
boss was strong and weak against. This brief adds a **post-battle results
dialog** on the hex map that presents that detail.

## Users

The **player** finishing a hex deployment in the Hangar War outer loop, and the
**attract/demo traversal** that must not stall on the new surface.

- As a player who won a hex, I want a dialog that tells me the outcome, my
  score and every reward I received, so I know exactly what the sortie earned me.
- As a player who lost a hex, I want a dialog that summarises the enemy boss's
  strengths and weaknesses (and the reward I missed), so I can plan the retake.
- As a player or watcher, I want to dismiss the dialog with one input (and have
  the attract demo auto-dismiss it) so the map stays playable and never stalls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a hex deployment ends, landing on `HexMapScene` presents a modal dialog over the paused map stating the battle outcome (`VICTORY`/`DEFEAT`) and the run's final score.
- On victory the dialog itemises every reward that was actually paid — salvage banked (minerals/cores), any granted weapon/upgrade, any special-mission reward, any contract and/or cache bonus, and the banked win bonus — and shows no line for a reward that was not paid.
- On defeat the dialog summarises the target hex boss's authored strengths and weaknesses (from `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`) and states the grant the player did not claim; it also states the unbanked salvage that was forfeited.
- The dialog is dismissible by a single confirm input (keyboard or pointer); dismissal resumes the map, and in demo/attract mode the dialog auto-dismisses after the shared dwell so the traversal cannot stall on it.
- The dialog's contents are produced by a shared, pure "result for view" builder over the game's own capture/defeat record and the authored hex definition (the dialog derives no reward or weakness itself), covered by unit tests plus a landing integration test that boots `HexMapScene` with a sortie result and asserts the dialog text and dismissal.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

After every hex battle the player gets one clear results dialog that names the
outcome, the rewards actually earned and, on a loss, the enemy's strengths and
weaknesses — so no sortie ends on a bare `RUN: DEFEAT` line with no explanation.

## Constraints

- **Reuse the shipped overlay pattern.** The map already pauses itself at the
  `SceneManager` level and launches `MiniBossWheelScene` / `MineralChoiceScene`
  over the paused map. The results dialog follows the same single-overlay
  contract (launch → pause → optional `onResult` callback → resume), including
  the demo auto-resolve rule (`HexMapScene.presentReward`).
- **One rule, no re-derivation.** Reward figures come from the capture cycle's
  own `HexCaptureResult` (`resolveHexCapture`) and the defeat path's
  `resolveDeploymentDefeat`; the boss strengths/weaknesses come from the authored
  hex definition. The dialog/view model must never re-derive a number.
- **Transient launch data only.** Like the existing run line, win bonus and
  assault banner, the sortie result is never persisted; a later menu/hangar
  re-entry shows no dialog.
- **Gym parity note.** `GymHexWar` is a read-only ring harness that runs no
  deployment and no combat, so it cannot show a post-battle dialog; this is a
  landing-surface presentation of the game's finished deployment, not a gameplay
  object, and needs no divergent gym copy.

## Risks

- **Handoff drift.** The reward detail lives in `HexCaptureResult`, not in the
  map today; if the handoff copies fields by hand, a new reward kind could be
  silently dropped from the dialog. Mitigation: pass the shipped record and let
  the pure builder read it, so a new reward field surfaces without a second edit.
- **Duplicated presentation.** If the dialog is added but the thin run line and
  win-bonus line are left in place, the landing shows the same facts twice.
  Mitigation: assumption A1 folds them in; a test asserts the dialog carries the
  outcome/score/win bonus.
- **Demo stall.** A modal that waits for input would freeze the attract
  traversal. Mitigation: reuse the existing demo auto-resolve rule so the dialog
  auto-dismisses after the shared dwell (asserted in a test).
- **Scope creep.** Related opportunities (e.g. surfacing the defeating bot's
  skills, or a full sortie history) are recorded as separate linked items rather
  than folded into this brief.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene` ends a hex deployment by starting `HexMapScene` with
  `{ payload, record, won, score, reward, assault, winBonusMinerals, demo,
  demoDwellMs }` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, the `_endRun` hangar-war branch).
- `HexMapScene` renders the map and a thin `runLine()`
  (`RUN: VICTORY|DEFEAT · score N`) plus the model's `winBonusLine` and, when a
  ring-end assault fired, the `RING WON` / `HANGAR FALLS` banner. It presents the
  mini-boss reward over the paused map via `presentReward()`.
- `HexCaptureResult` (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) already carries every
  reward number a victory paid: `bankedDelta`, `grant`, `specialReward`,
  `contractBonus`, `cachePayout`, `defender`, `ringSecured`, `ringAdvanced`,
  `assault`. The defeat path `resolveDeploymentDefeat` yields the `forfeited`
  salvage. **None of this is currently handed to the map** — only `assault`,
  `won`, `score` and `winBonusMinerals` are.
- Boss intel is authored per hex in `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`
  (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`): `boss`, `strengths`, `weaknesses`,
  `grants`, and is already surfaced in the map's detail panel.

## Desired change

1. Extend the deployment→map handoff so `HexMapScene` receives a compact
   **sortie result** for the finished deployment: the target hex id, the
   capture result's reward fields (`bankedDelta`, `grant`, `specialReward`,
   `contractBonus`, `cachePayout`, `ringSecured`, `ringAdvanced`) on a win, and
   `forfeited` on a loss (plus `won`/`score`/`winBonusMinerals`, already there).
2. Add a pure **results-for-view builder** (e.g.
   `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts`) that turns that record plus the authored
   hex definition into ordered dialog rows: outcome + score, every paid reward,
   and — only on defeat — the boss's strengths/weaknesses and the unclaimed
   grant. No rule lives in the scene.
3. Add the **results dialog overlay** (a new scene mirroring
   `MineralChoiceScene`'s pause/launch contract, or a modal section of the
   shared `hexMap` renderer) and present it on `HexMapScene.create()` when a
   sortie result is carried, before the demo dwell starts. A single confirm
   input dismisses it; demo auto-dismisses after the shared dwell.
4. Fold the now-redundant thin `runLine()` / win-bonus announcement into the
   dialog on a deployment landing (assumption A1), leaving the distinct
   hangar-assault banner in place.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — add the sortie result (capture/defeat record + target hex id) to the `scene.start(HEX_MAP_SCENE_KEY, …)` handoff at run end.

- `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.ts` (new, or extend `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) — pure results-for-view builder consuming the record + `HexRingDefinition`; the single source of dialog text.
- `src/scenes/HexCombatResultScene.ts` (new, or a modal section in `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`) — the pause/launch overlay with a single confirm dismissal, mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` / `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — types already carried (`HexCaptureResult`, `DeploymentDefeatResult`, `SalvageAmounts`); no rule change expected.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — authored `strengths`/`weaknesses`/`grants` read by the builder (no change expected).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/sortieResult.test.ts` (new) — coverage for the builder and the landing dialog.

# When completing first battle no minerals rewarded

## Problem statement

Today, a winning hangar battle that targets **no hex** — which is the first
battle of a fresh war, and the first battle after a war restart — shows
`WIN BONUS BANKED: +100 MINERALS` on the hex map, but nothing is banked: the
hangar still shows the same salvage balance, so the player is promised a reward
that never arrives.

## Root cause (evidence-backed)

The win-path bonus is banked by `PlayScene._resolveHangarWarCapture()`, which
**returns early** when the deployment has no hex:

```ts
// src/scenes/PlayScene.ts (≈4226)
const deployment = this.hangarWarDeployment;
if (!deployment || !deployment.hexId) return;   // ← no hex ⇒ no capture, no bonus
```

A fresh war stores an **empty ring** — `createDefaultPayload()` writes
`ring: { ringIndex: DEFAULT_RING_INDEX, hexes: [] }`
(`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`), and `restartHangarWar()` rebuilds that
same fresh payload (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`).

Only the **hex map** materialises the ring (`materialiseRing()` in
`src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`, persisted on first entry). The **hangar screen does
not**: `HangarScene.deploy()` builds the deployment from the raw stored payload,
so `selectDeploymentHex()` returns `null` for the empty ring and
`buildHangarDeployment()` records `hexId: null`
(`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`). The hangar's own DEPLOY row even
reads `▶ DEPLOY — no hex · aggression 0 · level 1`
(`formatRingLine` → `Ring 1 — 0/0 hexes held`).

The run itself is still a hangar-war run (`isHangarWarRun()` is true whenever a
deployment exists), so the mini-boss defeat ends on `_finaliseHangarWarMiniBossVictory`
→ `_resolveHangarWarCapture()` (no-op) → `_finishRun()` starts `HexMapScene`
with:

```ts
winBonusMinerals: won ? WIN_BONUS_MINERALS : 0,   // unconditional on `won`
```

The map renders `winBonusLine` from that value
(`src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` →
`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` → `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`), so the
announcement is decoupled from what was actually banked. The announcement is
**not** derived from the capture result — it is passed as a constant.

Consequence: the first hexless win banks **no bonus and no capture salvage**
(the capture cycle never runs), while the win screen claims +100 minerals.

Path evidence:
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_resolveHangarWarCapture()` early return (≈4228),
  `winBonusMinerals: won ? WIN_BONUS_MINERALS : 0` (≈5687).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — `hexId: hex?.id ?? null` from
  `selectDeploymentHex()` (returns `null` for an empty ring).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `createDefaultPayload()` empty ring.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — `deploy()` builds from the raw payload (no ring
  materialisation).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — the map materialises + persists the ring.

## Users

- **New player**: finishes the first battle after opening Hangar War, is told
  100 minerals were banked, then finds the hangar's salvage unchanged — the
  first reward of the outer loop appears broken.
- **Returning player who restarts the war**: sees the same mismatch on the new
  war's first battle.
- **Producer / balance owner**: needs the announced reward and the banked
  balance to agree in every path, because the win-bonus amount is a balance knob
  (`WIN_BONUS_MINERALS`).

User stories:

- As a new player, when I win my first battle, the minerals the win screen says
  I was awarded are in my hangar.
- As a player, I am never told a reward was banked unless it was actually banked.
- As a player, my first deployment targets a real hex (like every later
  deployment from the map), so my first win captures ground and grants the hex's
  authored entry.
- As a player on a save where the ring cannot be materialised, a winning battle
  still pays the fixed bonus — the run is a hangar deployment either way.

## Acceptance Criteria

Producer decisions recorded 2026-11-19 (Q1 = (a), Q2 = (a), Q3 = (a)) — see
Appendix. The first battle of a fresh war (and of a restarted war) now targets a
real hex and pays through the normal capture; the bonus-banking fallback exists
for a winning deployment that still has no target hex; and the announcement is
derived from what was actually banked.

- **Announcement ⇔ banking (Q3 = a).** A winning hangar battle never announces
  `WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS` unless that exact number was added to
  `hangar.bankedMinerals` in the same run resolution; the value the map renders
  is read from the win resolution's own record, not from
  `won ? WIN_BONUS_MINERALS : 0`.
- **Hexless win still pays (Q1 = a).** A winning hangar deployment with
  `hexId: null` banks exactly `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` (minerals only, capture
  watermark untouched, no hex state change), so the announced line and the
  hangar's salvage balance agree.
- **First deployment targets a real hex (Q2 = a).** A fresh war's ring is
  materialised from the authored definitions and persisted when the hangar
  screen loads its payload, so `▶ DEPLOY` names a real hex and the first battle
  banks its salvage + bonus through the normal capture cycle. The same holds
  after a war restart.
- **Exactly once.** A winning deployment pays the bonus once — the capture path
  when it ran, the fallback only when it did not; no path can pay both.
- **Regression tests.** A winning deployment with `hexId: null` asserts the
  announced bonus equals the actual `bankedMinerals` delta; a fresh-war hangar
  load asserts the ring is materialised, persisted and deployed at a real hex; a
  real-hex win asserts the captured balance is not topped up a second time.
- All existing hangar-war, capture-cycle, hex-map and win-bonus tests keep
  passing; the full project test suite passes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Impact

The first battle's reward is real: the minerals the win screen says were banked
are in the hangar, and the screen never claims a reward it did not pay.

## Constraints

- The win-bonus **amount** (`WIN_BONUS_MINERALS = CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT = 100`)
  is a provisional balance value baselined by `AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA`; this item
  must not change the number, only whether/what is announced.
- The win-path decisions recorded in `AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2` (producer Q1 = (c),
  Q2 = (a), Q3 = (b), 2026-11-13) stay authoritative: no mini-boss wheel, no
  bonus cores, minerals only, announced on the landing.
- The capture cycle remains the single authority for banking; a fix must not
  introduce a second write path or a new storage key.
- Demo/attract runs never persist — a demo hexless win must not write.
- Materialising the ring on hangar load is a **persisted** state change: it must
  go through `saveHangarWarPayload()`, respect the demo/storage guards already
  used by `HexMapScene.persist()`, and never pad or discard a partial ring.

## Interpretation of the producer's answers

Q1 = (a) and Q2 = (a) are complementary, not alternatives: the normal first
battle now targets a materialised hex, so it pays through the capture cycle;
Q1 = (a)'s "bank anyway" is the **fallback** for a winning deployment that still
has no target hex (an unauthored ring, or a save whose ring cannot be
generated). Payment is mutually exclusive: a capture that ran pays the bonus
itself, and the fallback pays only when no capture ran.

## Existing state

- Win bonus: `bankWinBonus()` (`src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts`), applied
  in `PlayScene._resolveHangarWarCapture()` only when a hex capture runs.
- Announcement: `winBonusMinerals` passed as run launch data to `HexMapScene`,
  rendered as `winBonusLine` in the `last-sortie` section.
- Ring materialisation exists (`materialiseRing()`) but is only used by
  `HexMapScene` (which persists it) and `resolveHexCapture()`;
  `HangarScene.loadPayload()` does not materialise, so a fresh war's DEPLOY is
  built from an empty ring.
- No test covers a winning deployment with `hexId: null`; every existing
  win-bonus test deploys at a real hex.

## Desired change

Per the producer's answers (Q1 = a, Q2 = a, Q3 = a):

1. **Ring materialisation at the hangar entry (Q2 = a)** — `HangarScene` loads
   its payload through `materialiseRing()` and persists the materialised ring
   (the `HexMapScene.init()` behaviour), so a fresh war's `▶ DEPLOY` targets a
   real hex and the first battle runs the normal capture cycle. Ring progress
   (`Ring 1 — 0/6 hexes held`) then reads correctly from the start.
2. **Bonus banking on a hexless win (Q1 = a)** — `_resolveHangarWarCapture()`
   gains a hexless winning branch that banks `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` through
   `bankWinBonus()` and persists it through the existing payload write, without
   touching the capture watermark and without inventing a hex capture.
3. **Announcement derived from the resolution (Q3 = a)** — the bonus the map
   announces comes from the win resolution's own record (the amount it banked),
   so an unbanked bonus can never be rendered and a double pay is impossible.
4. **Tests** for the three behaviours plus the existing suites, and the
   in-code notes beside `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` / `bankWinBonus()` updated to
   describe the hexless fallback.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — hexless winning branch in
  `_resolveHangarWarCapture()`; pass the banked amount (not the constant) to
  `HexMapScene` from `_finishRun()`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — materialise the ring on payload load and persist
  it; deploy from the materialised payload.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — reuse `materialiseRing()`; the capture
  rules themselves are unchanged.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — unaffected if the payload is
  already materialised; verify `hexId` resolves non-null.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — unchanged unless the launch-data field is
  renamed; the map keeps materialising for direct entries.
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` / `hangarEconomy.ts` — comment-only
  updates for the hexless fallback; `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` value unchanged.
- Tests: `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossVictory.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.captureCycle.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is unaffected (no gameplay object changes); the
  win-path notes live beside `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` and in
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** — Win path: suppress the mini-boss wheel and bank a
  fixed post-win bonus on hex wins (open, `plan_complete`; all children done).
  The originating design decision for the bonus this item exposes as mis-paid.
- **AH-0MWF2Q0O0008NGKL** — PlayScene: suppress win-path wheel and bank the
  bonus on win resolution (completed). Introduced the `won ? … : 0` announcement.
- **AH-0MWF2Q2JC008MAJE** — announce the banked win bonus before the map
  (completed). The surface that now over-claims.
- **AH-0MWL8CDGN005878A** — Owned hexes provide minerals (open). A separate
  income mechanic; not this bug.
- **AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA** — Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward
  value per hex deployment (completed). Owns the bonus amount.
- **AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6 / AH-0MWCOW4IQ003XST5** — capture cycle and mini-boss
  victory paths this bug runs through.
- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — a deployment ends on the hex map (the surface that
  shows the announcement).
- **AH-0MVUXC118004B4OX** — salvage banking at checkpoints (adjacent but not the
  same banking path).
- Duplicate check: no item already covers this defect; the automated
  related-work report below is complementary, not overlapping.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a hexless winning deployment is a defect, not a mode — once
  the hangar materialises the ring it should be unreachable in normal play and
  exists only for an unauthored/ungeneratable ring.
- **Risk — double pay:** the capture path and the new hexless fallback both pay
  the bonus; the implementation must make them mutually exclusive (a
  `banked`/`captured` flag on the win resolution), covered by the "exactly once"
  AC and a dedicated test.
- **Risk — scope creep:** "make the first battle pay", "capture a hex" and
  "fix the hangar's `0/0 hexes held` line" are three related changes; extra
  ring/UI polish belongs in linked items, not here.
- **Risk — double-counting:** any bonus banking added on the hexless path must
  stay outside the capture watermark (the reason `bankWinBonus()` is
  watermark-free) so a later checkpoint cannot re-bank.
- **Risk — demo writes:** an attract/demo run must still never persist a bonus
  (`_saveHangarWarPayload` demo guard).
- **Risk — test gaps:** the repo's scene tests fabricate deployments, so a
  `hexId: null` fixture must be added deliberately; otherwise the regression is
  invisible again.
- **Risk — stale balance display:** if the fix banks on the hexless path, the
  hangar must show the new balance when the map hands back (`openHangar` passes
  the map's payload, so no reload is expected).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Asked in a downtime-dispatched (non-interactive) intake session: the questions
were recorded on the work item with `needsProducerReview=true`, and the producer
answered in the follow-up session on 2026-11-19. The agent's recommendation is
recorded alongside each accepted answer for auditability.

### Q1 — What should a winning deployment with no target hex do? — Answer: **(a)**

Path context: a hangar `▶ DEPLOY` on a fresh war, or the first battle after a
war restart.

Options as asked: (a) bank the fixed bonus anyway on any winning deployment;
(b) bank nothing and show no bonus line; (c) materialise the ring so the first
battle always targets a real hex and pays through the capture cycle.

- Answer (producer, session reply 2026-11-19): **(a)**.
- Agent recommendation was (c) with (b) as a defensive guarantee; the producer
  chose the fallback-payment option instead. Q2 = (a) supplies the ring
  materialisation separately, so both effects land — see *Interpretation of the
  producer's answers*.

### Q2 — Where should a fresh war's ring be materialised? — Answer: **(a)**

Options as asked: (a) on hangar payload load, persisted (the hex map's
behaviour); (b) at deploy time only; (c) never.

- Answer (producer, session reply 2026-11-19): **(a)** — matches the agent
  recommendation.

### Q3 — Should the announcement be derived from the amount actually banked? — Answer: **(a)**

Options as asked: (a) yes, pass the banked delta; (b) keep the constant.

- Answer (producer, session reply 2026-11-19): **(a)** — matches the agent
  recommendation.

### Research recorded during intake

- The win-path decisions (`AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2`, producer 2026-11-13: Q1 = c,
  Q2 = a, Q3 = b) remain the governing design: no wheel, minerals only, bonus
  announced on the landing. This item changes **when** the bonus is banked and
  **what** is announced, not the amount.
- `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS` (= `CORE_MINERAL_EQUIVALENT` = 100) is a provisional
  balance value owned by `AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA`; it is not re-tuned here.

# Chime whenever a mineral is collected

## Problem statement

Collecting minerals — the game's core economy loop — is completely silent
today: `_collectMineral` credits the hold and updates the HUD bar, but the
player gets no audio confirmation at all. A successful mineral run therefore
feels flat, and the only confirmation is a small HUD bar the player is not
looking at during combat.

## Users

- **Player (game):** wants collecting minerals to feel rewarding and immediate
  without looking away from the ship.
  - *As a player, when my ship picks up a mineral I hear a quiet, satisfying
    chime so the pickup registers without me checking the HUD.*
  - *As a player, when I sweep up a scatter of minerals in quick succession
    the chime steps upward so a good run reads as rising musical momentum —
    and it settles back to its base note once I stop collecting.*
- **Maintainer / gym author:** needs the feedback to run the same code in the
  game and every gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity), with the pitch/level tuning
  in one place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every **player** mineral pickup plays a quiet chime: one chime per collected
  mineral, on every path that credits the mineral hold (`PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene` and its subclasses, `GymLevel`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` and
  the leveling gyms' mineral supply), through **one shared implementation** —
  no per-scene copy of the pitch/escalation logic.
- The chime **rises in pitch** with each successive pickup while the player
  keeps collecting, and **resets to its base pitch** after a gap of
  `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` (1.5 s) with no pickup; the rise is capped at a
  documented ceiling (A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]` semitones, i.e.
  up to one octave) so a long streak never becomes shrill.
- The chime is **subtle and quiet**: the baked asset peaks at ≤ 0.2 (the
  documented player-cue ceiling in GDD §7.3) with a stated target level in the
  recipe header, and it never masks enemy-fire telegraphs. It obeys the global
  SFX volume/mute settings and the shared per-cue voice limiter, and degrades
  to a silent no-op with no `AudioContext` (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
  browsers).
- **Enemy absorption plays no chime** — the feedback is player-only (an enemy
  hoovering up a mineral must not read as a player reward).
- New cue is delivered through the existing **ToneForge baked pipeline**: a new
  `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe (next free seed **32292**), a manifest entry, a
  deterministic baked WAV plus committed checksum, and `npm run
  build-audio:verify` passes unchanged for every pre-existing asset.
- The pitch-escalation state machine is **pure and unit-tested** with an
  injected clock: rise per pickup, cap, reset after the gap, and reset on
  run restart / scene teardown. A dense burst (several minerals in one frame,
  a 100-mineral gym field, Mineral Scoop sweep) is bounded — it may not
  shotgun-stack chimes beyond the shared voice limiter.
- Tests cover the cue (export + manifest + resolvable baked asset), the
  escalation state machine, and the shared wiring in the game and in the gyms.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (specifically
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` both tables and GDD §7.3 /
  §4.5).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Collecting minerals now rewards the ear as well as the HUD: each pickup gives a
quiet chime that steps upward through a quick scatter, so a mineral run feels
satisfying and audibly productive without the player ever glancing at the
mineral bar.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** the escalation rule and the cue dispatch live
  once; the game and every gym consume the same implementation. Divergence, if
  any (e.g. the leveling gyms' bespoke collection loops), must be justified in
  the work item and in a code comment.
- **Baked audio only:** no runtime synthesis. The cue must be a ToneForge
  recipe rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`, with SHA-256 checksums committed
  to `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json`; renders are deterministic (the pipeline
  renders twice and compares).
- **Enemy-balance guards are untouched:** the new recipe is a *player* cue, so it
  is tagged `player`/`mineral`/`pickup` with no enemy tag and no
  `AMPLITUDE_TIERS` key (the guard only analyses the enemy family). The A-minor
  conformance guard likewise applies to enemy cues only, but the pitch ladder is
  musical anyway so the cue sits inside the game's tonal language.
- **Player-cue ceiling** ≤ 0.2 peak (GDD §7.3), and every existing player cue
  degrades to a silent no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- **No second throttle:** the shared per-cue voice limiter (4 voices / 150 ms,
  `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`) already bounds overlap through the one
  `playCue` funnel; add no parallel rate limiter.
- **Reset gap is game time, not wall time**, so a paused scene cannot expire a
  streak mid-run and the streak does not depend on frame rate.
- **Purely audio:** no change to mineral economy, drop rules, collection
  geometry, scoring, telemetry or the hold model.
- No new persisted `rules.ts` tunable — pitch/level/length are fixed named
  constants beside the cue (precedent: `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES`,
  `WAVE_LASER_VOLUME_SCALE`), so retuning is a one-line change with no re-bake.
- Scope-creep guard: extra opportunities found on the way (e.g. a pitch ladder
  for power-up pickups, a streak HUD indicator) are recorded as separate linked
  work items, not folded into this one.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "slightly" means small steps — one A-minor scale degree per
  pickup, capped at an octave. If the producer prefers a chromatic ladder or a
  smaller cap, only `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES` changes.
- **Assumption:** the reset window is 1.5 s (`MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS`), the
  "short period" in the brief; one constant to retune.
- **Assumption:** a red 10-value deposit and a scattered pair each chime once
  per collected mineral, not once per mineral *unit*, so a deposit does not fire
  ten chimes.
- **Risk — aliasing:** reusing `aihell-mineral-tinkle` (the Mystery UFO spill
  cue) would make a pickup indistinguishable from a spill; mitigated by a
  dedicated `aihell-mineral-chime` recipe.
- **Risk — audio clutter:** mineral fields are dense (gyms seed 100 minerals,
  Mineral Scoop sweeps, doubled drops). Mitigated by the voice limiter, a quiet
  baked level and the cap on the pitch ladder; verified by a dense-burst test.
- **Risk — pitch/duration coupling:** raising pitch via `playbackRate` also
  shortens the cue (0.2 s → 0.1 s at the octave). Accepted (the countdown tick
  precedent) and documented in the recipe comment.
- **Risk — render environment:** baking needs the local ToneForge CLI
  (`../ToneForge`); if it is unavailable the implementer must not hand-write a
  WAV — stop and report the blocker.

## Existing state

- Collection seam: `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` (`collectMinerals`) is
  shared by `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility`; each scene supplies an `onPlayerCollected` callback
  (`_collectMineral` / `_collectGymMineral`) that credits the hold and syncs the
  HUD. `GymWeaponLeveling` / `GymPowerUpLeveling` run their own bespoke
  overlap loops over a seeded mineral supply.
- No pickup sound exists anywhere on those paths.
- `playMineralTinkleSound()` (`aihell-mineral-tinkle`, seed 32290) exists but is
  the Mystery UFO **spill** cue, fired once per spill with the scattered drops.
- Pitch escalation by playback rate already ships for the countdown tick:
  `playCountdownTickSound(step)` + `COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES` +
  `countdownTickRate(step)` (`src/audio/effects.ts`).
- One cue funnel: `playCue()` applies the per-cue voice limiter, seed variant
  pick and the shared master gain; `SfxPlayOptions` supports `rate`, `volume`,
  `delay`, `loop`.
- The seed block 32100–32299 is reserved for game recipes; the highest shipped
  seed is 32291, so **32292** is the next free seed.
- Contract tests (`src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`) fail if an `effects.ts` cue has no
  manifest entry or no baked asset — a new cue cannot ship half-wired.

## Desired change

1. **New baked cue** `aihell-mineral-chime` — a short (~0.2 s, ≤ 0.2 peak)
   bright chime: one triangle/sine partial with a gentle decay and a quiet
   shimmer, deliberately distinct from `aihell-mineral-tinkle` (no falling
   E7 → A6 sweep, no noise tick) so a pickup never reads as a spill. Recipe,
   manifest entry (seed 32292), baked WAV, checksum.
2. **`playMineralCollectChimeSound()`** in `src/audio/effects.ts` — plays the
   cue at the current streak step's rate, with the semitone ladder, cap and gap
   as named constants.
3. **Shared escalation state machine** — a small Phaser-free module (e.g.
   `src/audio/mineralChime.ts`) owning the streak counter, the game-clock gap
   check and the reset, with an injectable clock for deterministic tests. One
   exported `noteMineralCollected(nowMs)` that advances the step and returns the
   playback rate, plus a reset seam for run restart / scene teardown.
4. **Wiring** — every player-collection path calls the shared seam exactly once
   per collected mineral (preferably from the shared collection layer or one
   shared core hook rather than five copies).
5. **Docs** — recipe header, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (mapping
   table + new-recipes table), GDD §7.3 cue table and the §4.5 collection
   bullet, plus the code comments recording the pitch-ladder and gap rationale.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` — New shared escalation state machine
  (streak step, cap, 1.5 s game-clock gap, reset seam; injectable clock).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — New `playMineralCollectChimeSound()` plus the
  semitone-ladder/gap constants beside the cue.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — Shared collection seam; preferred single
  dispatch point for the player-pickup chime.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_collectMineral` (game path; must not duplicate
  the escalation logic).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_collectMineral` (every
  formation gym).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  — Remaining player-collection paths / bespoke mineral loops.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — Candidate shared hook if the dispatch
  belongs on the scene core instead of the collection layer.
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-mineral-chime.yaml` — New recipe (seed
  32292; document the level target and the rate/aliasing rationale).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — New cue entry.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-mineral-chime.32292.wav`,
  `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — Baked asset + checksum
  (`npm run build-audio`).
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`
  (§7.3 cue table, §4.5 collection bullet) — Documentation rows/rationale.
- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` (new), `src/audio/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Coverage for the state
  machine, cue wiring and the defined-once/parity guards.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-19)

Decomposed into six child items, **test-first and dependency-ordered**. Each
child carries its own acceptance criteria, minimal implementation slice and
key files; this block is the traceability index only.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|-----------|
| 1 | Mineral chime escalation spec tests (AH-0MWNMRBO4000T5F8) | task | — |
| 2 | Pure mineral chime escalation state machine (AH-0MWNMRCEW006N0EH) | task | 1 |
| 3 | Baked aihell-mineral-chime cue (AH-0MWNMRD6I002CCVT) | task | 2 |
| 4 | One shared chime dispatch on every player pickup (AH-0MWNMRDY60005Z4K) | feature | 2, 3 |
| 5 | Document the mineral pickup chime (AH-0MWNMRER0009385Y) | docs | 4 |
| 6 | Verify the mineral chime end to end (AH-0MWNMRFJ9004F66R) | task | 4, 5 |

**Phase plan — each phase is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs/infra):**

1. **Pitch rule** (items 1→2): the pure state machine and the spec that drives
   it — behaviour, unit tests and documented constants land together.
2. **Audible cue** (item 3): recipe → deterministic bake → committed WAV +
   checksum → manifest entry → `effects.ts` export → contract and peak tests.
3. **Gameplay wiring** (item 4): the single shared core dispatch plus the six
   collection paths and the run-reset/teardown resets, with the parity,
   absorption-silence, defined-once and dense-burst tests.
4. **Docs** (item 5): cue-mapping tables, GDD §7.3/§4.5, README, code comments,
   pinned by a docs assertion test.
5. **Verification gate** (item 6): `build-audio:verify`, the full suite via the
   test skill, the production build and the ear check.

**Between phases:** re-read the next child's description and update it with
anything the previous slice learned (final constant names, cue name, test seams
to extend) before starting it. The children are the implementable
specification; this item's ACs are the coverage map.

**Architecture decision (recorded, no producer input needed):** the single
dispatch point is a shared `CombatCoreScene` hook, **not** the Phaser-free
`mineralLayer.collectMinerals`. Rationale, consequences and the parity argument
are in the wiring child's "Architecture decision" section.

**Plan changelog:** 2026-11-19 — first decomposition: 6 children created (issue
types task/task/task/feature/docs/task), 7 dependency edges wired, six automated
review stages run, AC coverage review = `proceed`. No prior plan block existed.

## Related work

- **Mystery UFO feel layer** (AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6) and its cue bake
  (AH-0MVSAJMLL00835T8) — shipped `aihell-mineral-tinkle` for the UFO **spill**,
  the closest existing mineral audio and the reason a pickup cue must not alias
  it.
- **Countdown count SFX cue via the ToneForge pipeline** (AH-0MV55OA93008OUL1)
  — the precedent for rising pitch through playback `rate` (`COUNTDOWN_TICK_SEMITONES`,
  `countdownTickRate`) and for adding a recipe/manifest/checksum/docs in one
  change.
- **Wire non-combat pickup audio into `GymPowerUps._collectDrop()`**
  (AH-0MTGS94T9007TAAC), **PlayScene: add per-type power-up pickup activation
  audio** (AH-0MU8QVX9G008P8ML) and **Pop SFX** (AH-0MUBYSNGU0051XVO) — the
  established pickup-feedback convention this item extends to minerals.
- **Mineral collectable entity and constants** (AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT), **Shared
  mineral layer** (AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF) and **Red mineral deposits**
  (AH-0MVJ79739008396I) — the collection/value semantics the chime must not
  change (a deposit pays one chime, one 10-value pickup).
- **SFX mix** (AH-0MVZVMZOQ00076QF) — the family-trim mechanism
  (`*_VOLUME_SCALE` named constants) that a quieter chime should follow rather
  than re-baking assets.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake ran from an **automated downtime dispatch** (no interactive producer
present), so the three feel-tuning choices below could not be answered in
session. Each records the **recommended option** that the brief has adopted as
its documented default, the evidence behind it, and an **OPEN QUESTION** marker
so the producer can override any of them without re-planning (each is a single

Part of **Chime whenever a mineral is collected** (AH-0MWNHEIV90047V91). Owns
the streak counter, the reset-gap check and the pitch ladder **once**, in a
Phaser-free module with an injected clock, so the game and every gym share the
rule and the tuning lives in one place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` exists and exports:
  - `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES` — the A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]`,
    documented as "one scale degree per pickup, capped at one octave";
  - `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` — `1500`, documented as **game time** (scene
    clock), not wall time;
  - `mineralChimeRate(step)` — `2 ** (semitones / 12)` for a clamped step
    (precedent: `countdownTickRate` in `src/audio/effects.ts`);
  - `noteMineralCollected(nowMs)` — advances the streak (or restarts it when
    the gap expired) and returns the **playback rate** to play;
  - `resetMineralChimeStreak()` — the run-restart / scene-teardown seam;
  - `mineralChimeStep()` — current step, for observability and tests.
- The module imports nothing from `scenes/`, `Phaser`, or `audio/effects`, and
  reads no wall clock (`Date.now`/`performance.now`); every time value comes
  from the caller.
- Behaviour matches the sibling spec item exactly (all its cases green).
- The module records, in comments, why the ladder is A-minor scale degrees,
  why the cap is an octave, and why the gap is game time (a paused scene must
  not expire a streak mid-run).
- No new persisted `rules.ts` tunable is introduced (fixed named constants).
- The chime rises in pitch with each successive pickup while the player keeps collecting, and resets to its base pitch after a gap of `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` (1.5 s) with no pickup; the rise is capped at a documented ceiling (A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]` semitones, up to one octave) so a long streak never becomes shrill.

3. Reset when `nowMs - lastPickupMs > MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS`.

- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` — the spec it must satisfy.

# One shared chime dispatch on every player pickup

Part of **Chime whenever a mineral is collected** (AH-0MWNHEIV90047V91). Wires
the cue into gameplay **once**: one shared dispatch point in the combat core,
consumed by the game and every gym, so no scene keeps a copy of the escalation
rule (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `CombatCoreScene` owns the single dispatch: one `protected` method (e.g.
  `noteMineralCollected()`) that reads the scene clock (`this.time.now`, game
  time — pauses with the scene, never wall time), advances the shared state
  machine and plays `playMineralCollectChimeSound(step)` exactly once.
- Every **player** collection path calls that one method exactly once per
  collected mineral — `PlayScene._collectMineral`,
  `GymFormationScene._collectMineral` (and every formation-gym subclass
  through it), `GymLevel._collectMineral`,
  `GymPowerUpsUtility._collectGymMineral`, and the bespoke leveling loops
  `GymWeaponLeveling._collectMineralsOverlapping` /
  `GymPowerUpLeveling._collectMineralsOverlapping`.
- **Enemy absorption is silent**: a mineral absorbed by an enemy entity plays
  no chime, asserted in the game and in a gym (the feedback is player-only).
- The streak is reset in the shared `resetRunState()` **and**
  `teardownRunState()` seams, so a restarted run and a scene shutdown both
  start from the base pitch (the scene instance is reused across restarts).
- A repo-wide guard test (using `collectProductionSourceFiles` from
  `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts`) proves the ladder/gap/cue reference exists
  in exactly **one** production site — no scene re-implements the escalation
  or calls `playMineralCollectChimeSound` directly.
- A dense-burst test collects many minerals in one frame (a scattered pair, a
  Mineral Scoop sweep and a 100-mineral gym field) and asserts the shared voice
  limiter bounds the admitted voices (`MAX_CONCURRENT_CUE_VOICES`) with no
  throw and no second throttle.
- A gym↔game parity test boots the real `PlayScene` and a real gym, collects a
  mineral in each, and observes the same cue dispatch (no scene-local
  divergence); `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is updated only if a divergence is
  introduced (expected: none — every scene inherits the shared core).
- The collection/economy behaviour is unchanged: no mineral value, drop rule,
  collection geometry, scoring or telemetry change (existing tests stay green).
- Every player mineral pickup plays a quiet chime — one chime per collected mineral, on every path that credits the mineral hold, through one shared implementation — so a `PlayScene` run and any gym behave identically.
- Enemy absorption plays no chime — the feedback is player-only, so an enemy hoovering up a mineral never reads as a player reward.

## Minimal implementation

1. Add the shared dispatch method + the two resets to
   `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`.
2. Add the single call in each of the six collection paths (one line each —
   no logic).
3. Add the wiring, absorption-silence, reset and dense-burst tests; add the
   defined-once guard case to the parity guard test file.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared dispatch + run-reset/teardown resets.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — one call per player collection path.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralChime.parity.test.ts` (new) — shared-dispatch, absorption-silence, reset and defined-once guards.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — existing wiring/equivalence guards.

## Architecture decision (recorded, no producer input needed)

The brief offered two candidate single dispatch points: the shared collection
layer (`src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`) or a shared core hook
(`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`). **This item uses the shared core hook.**

Why: `collectMinerals` is deliberately Phaser-free (`@module
scenes/core/mineralLayer`) and is consumed by the headless eval arena tests
(`src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts`); firing audio from it would inject a
side effect into the pure collection layer and leave the two bespoke leveling
gyms' own overlap loops uncovered anyway. Every player-collection path in the
game and in the gyms extends `CombatCoreScene` (`PlayScene`, `GymLevel`,
`GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymPowerUpLeveling` via `CombatScene`;
`GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` directly), so a hook there covers
all six paths with one line each, gets the scene clock (`this.time.now`, game
time) for free, and reuses the existing `resetRunState()` /
`teardownRunState()` seams for the streak reset — no new lifecycle hook.

This is a deliberate, documented narrowing of the brief's "preferably from the
shared collection layer": the escalation *logic* still lives exactly once (in
`src/audio/mineralChime.ts` + the one core hook), which is the parity rule that
matters; only the six call sites are per-scene, and the defined-once guard test
above enforces that they carry no logic.

## Dependencies

Depends on **Pure mineral chime escalation state machine** and **Baked
aihell-mineral-chime cue**. Blocks the documentation item.

# Reconcile arena moving-hostile profiles with the class models and fix the chaser over-dodge

**Raised by:** AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT (seeded per-class avoidance sweep).
**Blocks:** AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT — the sweep cannot satisfy its pass bar until this lands.
**Priority:** high (epic AH-0MWLUIOH9001XBJ3 acceptance evidence).

## Problem

The seeded per-class sweep over the headless arena (Feature 6's moving-hostile
opt-in, live competent brain, `hazardMotionModelEnabled` on/off, 12 seeds,
1800 ticks, 4 immortal single-class bodies, 2 minerals) measures **avoidable**
enemy-body contacts (a contact is avoidable when a 16-direction escape fan at
`playerSpeed` clears the contact radius from the body's fitted velocity 0.25 s
before the overlap). Measured with the arena's shipped class profiles:

| class | contacts off | contacts on | seeds better / worse / tie | aggregate off→on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chaser | 46 | 39 | 5 / 0 / 7 | −15% |
| diver | 79 | 47 | 9 / 0 / 3 | −41% |
| patroller | 19 | 21 | 4 / 4 / 4 | +11% |
| formation (control) | 10 | 26 | 1 / 5 / 6 | +160% |
| roamer (control) | 22 | 20 | 2 / 1 / 9 | −9% |

The AC's bar (curving classes strictly fewer on a **majority** of seeds;
`roamer`/`formation` **never increase**) is therefore not met: `chaser` reduces
but only on 5/12 seeds, `patroller` is flat, and both controls increase on some
seeds. The 60 Hz scripted-curving proof in
`src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` (off: min distance 25.7 px, inside the
30 px contact radius; on: 39.2 px, clear) shows the model *does* work when the
scripted trajectory matches the class model — so the failure is in the harness /
live closed-loop interaction, not in the sampler's core idea.

## Diagnosis

1. **Harness and predictor disagree about the class semantics.** Feature 6's
   arena profiles are a sinusoidal `patroller` weave and a circular `formation`
   sway (`hostileMotionVelocity`), while the predictor's class models are
   `patroller` = straight patrol then straight commit and `formation` = linear
   drift + edge reflection (`src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts`). The sweep
   is validating each predictor against a trajectory it does not model.
   Re-running with the arena profile temporarily changed to the predictor's
   semantics made both classes neutral-to-better (patroller aggregate 58→51,
   89→81; formation 23→19, 13→12), confirming the mismatch.
2. **The chaser over-dodges.** With the model on, a pursuing chaser is predicted
   to threaten every bearing; `planSteering` picks the least-bad escape, which
   keeps the ship near the body, and rising-edge contacts increase (the control
   arm flies its line and often finishes with one contact per body). This is the
   behaviour the pinned note in `hazardMotionModel.test.ts` warned about.
3. **The metric is coarse.** With 4 immortal bodies, contacts saturate at one
   per body, so per-seed comparisons are dominated by ties. Any fix should
   either raise the encounter rate (fast crossing geometry) or measure at a
   finer granularity while keeping the AC's per-seed rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- The arena's moving-hostile class profiles and the predictor's class models
  describe the **same** trajectory semantics, asserted by a test (a class
  profile the predictor does not model must fail that test).
- The chaser sweep arm no longer regresses: a live competent bot with the
  motion model on records **no more** avoidable contacts than the
  constant-velocity control on any seed, and strictly fewer on a majority.
- The seeded per-class sweep (`src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts`) lands
  green with the AC bar: `chaser`/`diver`/`patroller` strictly fewer avoidable
  contacts on a majority of a documented seed list; `roamer`/`formation` never
  increase. A failure names the offending seed and class.
- With that evidence, flip `COMPETENT_BOT_TUNABLES.hazardMotionModelEnabled` to
  `true`, update the pin in `hazardMotionModel.test.ts` (with the evidence
  reference, not silently), and re-baseline any eval expectation the flip
  genuinely moves, recording the rationale.

## Evidence / artefacts

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the moving mode now exposes each hostile's stable
  `id`/`movementClass` on the bot snapshot (only under the opt-in), which the
  tracker needs to fit a velocity at all.
- `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` — the 60 Hz scripted-curving proof.
- Measurement harness and per-seed numbers reproducible from the described
  scenario (recorded on AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT).

**Key files:** `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts`,
`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`, `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`,
`src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts` (new), `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts`.
## Impact

The shipped bot now dodges *curving* enemies — a chasing ghost, a committing diver, a raider breaking into its attack run — instead of flying into where they were, and it no longer hovers beside a pursuer: across the documented seed list the motion model cuts avoidable enemy-body contacts for every curving class (chaser 255→92, patroller 248→89, diver 172→113) while leaving straight-line hazards provably untouched.

## Outcome (AH-0MWOKL79Z0051ZXO)

All four ACs met, and `hazardMotionModelEnabled` now ships **on**.

- **AC1 — one trajectory definition.** `advanceHazardMotion` is the single implementation of each movement class. The arena's moving-hostile mode advances its live bodies through that same call (the old sinusoidal `patroller` weave, circular `formation` sway, pulsing `diver` and its `elapsed`/`phase` clock are gone), and an unknown class throws. `arena.test.ts` pins the identity and asserts a profile the model does not know fails.
- **AC2 — the chaser arm no longer regresses.** Root cause was the chaser model: a constant-turn-rate arc fitted from the last two position deltas predicted an orbit a pursuing ghost never flies, and once close it read as a threat on every escape bearing, so the fan had no direction to prefer. The chaser is now pure pursuit (the shipped `steerToward` re-aims every frame), it no longer earns a curvature horizon boost (its own turn is already modelled), and its per-class window is the configured horizon — the 1.6 window was what made `promo-ghost-hunt` kite instead of fight. Sweep: 10/12 seeds strictly better, 0 regressions.
- **AC3 — the seeded sweep is green.** `src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts`: 12 documented seeds, 1800 ticks, live competent brain, model off vs on, avoidable enemy-body contacts. chaser 255→92 (10 better/0 worse), diver 172→113 (8/3), patroller 248→89 (8/1), roamer 191→191 (0/0, bit-identical — a straight class path returns the fixed-velocity solve exactly), formation 58→55 (2/0). A failure names the seed and class, and the table is printed.
- **AC4 — flipped with evidence.** `COMPETENT_BOT_TUNABLES.hazardMotionModelEnabled` is `true`; the pin in `hazardMotionModel.test.ts` records the sweep evidence; `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.10 is updated. No eval expectation needed re-baselining: the full suite (including the real-game `src/scenes/PromoScenarioSurvival.integration.test.ts`, whose 45 s target was **not** relaxed) is green with the model live.
